AGP Notes:
How are hydrosols made? The distillation process involves filling the still with plant material and forcing pressurized steam through the plant. The pressurized steam breaks open the cells to release the oil content. The steam and oil molecules pass through a cooling condenser, turning the steam back to water.

The water is collected in a Florentine flask and the oil generally floats on the surface of the water. This water is the hydrosol.

Lavender Hydrosol is a personal favorite. I use it for all kinds of skin issues for myself and my animals, as it is cleansing, cooling and offers an anti-inflammatory effect for the skin.  I also use it to clean! I spray it on any surface that tolerates water, such as my windows, glass tables, kitchen counters and just about everywhere in the bathroom!

Shelf life: 1 year from production (keep cool)

Aldehyde­-rich oils are sensitive to oxidation, and best stored in a refrigerator to achieve the longest possible shelf life.

It's best to use aldehyde-­rich oils well­ diluted and in low doses, as they may irritate skin and mucous membranes. Avoid using with sensitive or damaged skin. Tisserand recommends maximum dermal level of 0.8%.

Oils containing citral should be avoided with antidepressants (specifically Bupropion) that inhibit CYP2B6 enzyme. Robert Tisserand states that this risk is considered "theoretical" based on the research.

Oils containing citral (Lemongrass, May Chang, Honey Myrtle, Lemon Myrtle) should not be used orally with antidiabetic medication.

AGP Notes:
As you know, essential oils and water do not mix. When essential oils are added into a water or hydrosol spray, the tiny droplets of essential oil stay separate from the water/hydrosol. When sprayed on the body we get tiny droplets of neat essential oil on our skin. To evenly disperse essential oil into the water/hydrosol we use "Solubol.” It works great to protect the skin from neat essential oil, and has a very mild aroma that doesn't seem to influence the aroma of the blend. We most often use Solubol in sprays we make for damaged or sensitive skin.

There is some debate about how much Solubol one needs to fully disperse essential oil into the water. The range seems to go from 1:1 ratio (1 drop Solubol to 1 drop essential oil), to 1:8 (8 drops Solubol to 1 drop essential oil). We use it at a 1:4 ratio (1 drop essential oil to 4 drops Solubol).

Soluble is an all-natural product, here are the ingredients:

Sucrose Stearate – An emulsifier made from sugar and vegetable oil
Helianthus annus – Annual sunflower oil
Cera alba – Beeswax
Sterculia urens – A medium-sized, deciduous tree that exudes a gum called karaya used in food as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener
The gum of the acacia tree
Propolis Wax from bees
